headline: Joint Subspace Sparse Attention reports long-context decoding gains in author-run benchmarks
summary: The Oct. 13 preprint introduces Joint Subspace Sparse Attention (JSSA), a training-free token-level sparse-attention method that combines a shared query–key scoring subspace with gather-free indexed attention. In author-run tests on one NVIDIA B200 at 128K context with 2,048 selected KV tokens, the paper reports up to 1.51× full-KV decoding throughput on Qwen3-8B, 1.88× on Gemma4-26B-A4B-It, and 6.43× on GLM-4.7-Flash. The authors report accuracy near full-KV on the tested tasks and provide an implementation and benchmark scripts. These are paper-reported results; the research desk did not reproduce them.
